messages.author: ca3205004f4bea24
messages.subject: Can't deploy an app with 'devtools' installed locally
parts:
I'm pretty sure I followed all the instructions in https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps/blob/master/guide/guide.md. System is Fedora Linux 20 Beta, R 3.0.2, RStudio Preview 0.98.482. I

1. Created a Shiny Apps project directory using RStudio
2. Installed 'devtools' as described.
3. Restarted the R Session
4. Created the 'Diamond Explorer' app.
5. Ran the app locally. Note for Linux users - if you're a KDE desktop user, the app may come up in the Konqueror browser, and as of a few minutes ago, the graph didn't show up in Konqueror. However, the app *does* work in Firefox 25. The same is true for the HTML help in RStudio; if you use KDE you'll probably want to change your desktop settings to use Firefox, Chromium or Chrome.
6. OK - now to deploy the app. When I typed 'deployApp()' it threw the following error:

> library(shinyapps)
> deployApp()
Preparing to deploy application...DONE
Uploading application bundle...
Error: Unable to deploy package dependency 'devtools'

The package was installed locally from source. Only packages installed from CRAN or GitHub are supported.
>

I'm pretty sure I installed 'devtools' first from CRAN and then from Github. I'm going to try re-installing it, though.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Re: Can't deploy an app with 'devtools' installed locally
parts:
Edward,

From the looks of this, you're still running the version of devtools from CRAN (1.3). The latest version of devtools from GitHub is 1.4. Using a version of devtools < 1.4 will prevent packages installed from GitHub from working when deployed to shinyapps. Would you mind updating devtools and seeing if you are able to run deployApp()?


devtools::install_github('devtools', 'hadley')

(restart your R session)

parts:
Ed,

I think it sounds like it's working correctly: 

When deployApp() is called, we detect all your application dependencies. This list of packages and your application code gets bundled and uploaded to the server. We then build the list packages specified in the bundle. The package binaries then cached on a per-application basis (that is why subsequent calls to deployApp() will not require any packages to be built). When the image is created, only cached packages from the current bundle are installed into the R library.

-Andy
